headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make CrewAI→Kestra interactions dangerous by default, with cascading automation and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and Kestra reads/writes /app/storage and /tmp, so a shared filesystem bridge can let attacker-controlled content flow from one agent into the other. Neither profile shows provenance tracking or isolation by default, so prompt-like content in files can hijack downstream interpretation.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Kestra ingests files produced by CrewAI as workflow inputs
mitigations: Separate the working directories immediately
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add a provenance header check before parsing any file
Run each agent in a container with distinct mounts
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Kestra can move logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications over broad network surfaces. If they share a workspace, sensitive data touched by CrewAI can be copied into Kestra outputs or external services without a default guardrail.
conditions: IF CrewAI receives secrets or sensitive crew inputs
IF Kestra is configured to publish logs, notifications, or artifacts externally
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared files
Restrict Kestra notifications to a test sink
Rotate any API keys used by CrewAI
Limit both agents to a private workspace
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and network egress. CrewAI explicitly lacks self-isolation by default, while Kestra exposes root and docker.sock privileges. Running them against the same mutable resources creates a strong write-write conflict and can corrupt files, jobs, or infrastructure state.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or repository
IF Kestra tasks and CrewAI tools mutate shared state concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable root and docker.sock for the test run
Run one agent at a time
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework with shared memory, and Kestra is a declarative workflow engine that can trigger tasks, notifications, and external actions. That makes it plausible for CrewAI output to be treated as authoritative input to Kestra, causing unverified facts to cascade into emails, jobs, or infrastructure actions.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes CrewAI-generated text as workflow parameters
IF Kestra tasks act on CrewAI outputs without validation
mitigations: Insert a human approval step
Validate CrewAI outputs against a schema
Mark CrewAI output as untrusted in Kestra
Disable auto-triggered notifications for the test
requires-engineering: add verification gates before actions

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI is documented as handling developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Kestra can route logs, artifacts, cloud storage data, and notifications across many external services. The pair can therefore create retention and residency mismatches on the same data class, even though no specific HIPAA/GDPR claim is documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared workflows
IF Kestra retention or notification targets differ from CrewAI handling
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Shorten Kestra retention settings
Disable external notifications
Document the data flow and residency
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
